anchor_definition: The anchor is the LEx command `execute` method, whose body constructs the s, t and o signature parameters (when isApiV2) and appends them to the request URL before sending the ajax request. The signature is built inline (no separate helper); execute is the function that produces the observed s/t/o. Generic param/data setters are decoys.

anchor.why: Builds curUrl, and under this.isApiV2 derives sig (s), the keyed timestamp (t) and tkey (o) from chars/Math.random/Date.parse, appends ?s=&t=&o= to the URL, and issues the ajax request. This is where the observed s/t/o signature parameters are generated.

roles.why: Hezhun (approval) paging submit handler (the qrCheck().then callback): builds the LEx.Command, sets page/rows/projectType params and calls cmd.execute("getBusinessListByProjectCode") — the call site that triggers the observed request. A path/wrapper that dispatches the anchor; it does not itself construct s/t/o.

Beian (record-filing) paging submit handler (the qrCheck().then callback): equivalent call site to onQueryHezhun — builds the command, sets params and calls cmd.execute("getBusinessListByProjectCode"). A path/wrapper that dispatches the anchor; it does not itself construct s/t/o.

The Command constructor: sets this.isApiV2 = true (the exact flag whose truthiness gates the s/t/o branch inside execute) and builds this.url/this.action/this.paramsObj — the request scaffolding execute reads when constructing curUrl. Path-critical setup, but it does not itself derive s/t/o.

Generic null/empty predicate invoked inside the s/t/o branch (if(!LEx.isNotNull(__signature))) and by the Command constructor. A reusable low-level helper on the path, not specific to signature construction.
Stores a request parameter on the command object; trims strings. Not on the s/t/o signature path.
Copies a data object onto the command; not involved in signature generation.

Promise wrapper that forwards to this.execute(type,false,cb). It would relay an s/t/o request, but it has zero call sites in the capture (the observed paging uses synchronous cmd.execute) — a tempting same-name decoy that is not on this observable's path.

Generic MD5 primitive from the bundled md5.js. The s/t/o signature is built from Math.random/Date.parse, not hashed — this is the strongest 'is the signature a digest?' decoy, off-chain for this observable.

empty_roles.reason: No helper is dedicated to building part of s/t/o. The signature (sig, the key/tkey derivation loops, the keyed timestamp) is constructed entirely inline inside execute as straight-line statements — there is no nested function below the anchor to award 0.7. (The original azdg.encrypt helper for t is present but commented out: `t = timestamp;//LEx.azdg.encrypt(...)`, so it is off-path.)

The s/t/o construction uses only Math.random, Date.parse and String methods (builtins) — no crypto/encoding primitive (md5/AES/RSA/SM/base64/uuid) is on the construction path, so there is no Core-utility tier to award. The bundled md5/crypto-js primitives are off-chain decoys (score 0), not 0.5, because the signature is random/time-derived rather than hashed. Matches README §'Coarse score gradient' for real captures.
